message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.008 u (average; protium = 1.007825 u) |
| **Isotopes** | Protium (^1H), Deuterium (^2H), Tritium (^3H) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Electron affinity** | 0.754 eV (72.8 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) |
| **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ |
| **Molecular weight (H₂)** | 2.016 g mol⁻¹ |
| **State at room temperature** | Colorless, odorless, tasteless gas |
| **Bond type** | Diatomic covalent (H–H) |
| **Reactivity** | Highly flammable; reacts with oxygen (combustion), halogens, acids, and many metals (forming hydrides) |
| **Uses** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells, rockets), industrial feedstock (ammonia, methanol, hydrogenation reactions), metallurgy, cryogenics, medical imaging (deuterated water), etc. |
| **Physical behavior** | Forms weak van der Waals forces; no permanent dipole moment; can form hydrogen bonds when bonded to electronegative atoms (e.g., in water). |
| **Magnetic moment** | 1.410 µB (protium) |
| **Nuclear spin** | ½ (protium), 0 (deuterium), ½ (tritium) |

These values capture the essential physical, chemical, and nuclear characteristics that define hydrogen as the simplest and most abundant element in the universe.
